Everything here is free to read or use online. Each entry says which of my [tutorials](tutorials.qmd), articles or projects it goes with, so you can go deeper on the part you're working on.

## Free books

::: {.grid .resource-grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pub-card}
[R · tidyverse]{.pub-year}

[[R for Data Science (2nd edition)](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/)]{.pub-title}

[Hadley Wickham, Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel and Garrett Grolemund]{.pub-meta}

The place to start with R: importing, tidying, transforming and visualising data with the tidyverse.

Goes with: [Tutorial 1: Importing data](tutorials/01-import-data-in-r/import-data-in-r.qmd) and [Tutorial 3: Cleaning data](tutorials/03-clean-data-in-r/clean-data-in-r.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pub-card}
[R · figures]{.pub-year}

[[ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis (3rd edition)](https://ggplot2-book.org/)]{.pub-title}

[Hadley Wickham, Danielle Navarro and Thomas Lin Pedersen]{.pub-meta}

How ggplot2 works, from the grammar of graphics to scales, facets and themes. The online third edition is still being written.

Goes with: the figures in [Choosing the right statistics for cytokine data](writing/choosing-statistics-for-cytokine-data/index.qmd) and every tutorial
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pub-card}
[Statistics]{.pub-year}

[[Introductory Statistics for the Life and Biomedical Sciences](https://www.openintro.org/book/biostat/)]{.pub-title}

[Julie Vu and David Harrington (OpenIntro)]{.pub-meta}

An introduction to statistics built on biomedical examples. The PDF is free (you can set the price to $0).

Goes with: [Tutorial 4: Statistical tests](tutorials/04-statistical-tests-in-r/statistical-tests-in-r.qmd) and the [guide to choosing a test](guides/choosing-a-statistical-test/choosing-a-statistical-test.pdf)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pub-card}
[Statistics]{.pub-year}

[[Introduction to Modern Statistics (2nd edition)](https://openintrostat.github.io/ims/)]{.pub-title}

[Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel and Johanna Hardin (OpenIntro)]{.pub-meta}

A modern introduction that teaches randomisation and bootstrapping alongside the classical tests.

Goes with: [Tutorial 4: Statistical tests](tutorials/04-statistical-tests-in-r/statistical-tests-in-r.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pub-card}
[Statistics · R]{.pub-year}

[[APS 240: Data Analysis and Statistics with R](https://dzchilds.github.io/stats-for-bio/)]{.pub-title}

[Dylan Z. Childs, Bethan J. Hindle and Philip H. Warren]{.pub-meta}

A university course book that teaches statistics and R together for biologists, with clear chapters on assumptions, transformations and paired designs.

Goes with: [Tutorial 4: Statistical tests](tutorials/04-statistical-tests-in-r/statistical-tests-in-r.qmd) and [Choosing the right statistics for cytokine data](writing/choosing-statistics-for-cytokine-data/index.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pub-card}
[Python · pandas]{.pub-year}

[[Python for Data Analysis (3rd edition)](https://wesmckinney.com/book/)]{.pub-title}

[Wes McKinney]{.pub-meta}

Data wrangling in Python with pandas and NumPy, by the creator of pandas. Free to read online.

Goes with: [Tutorial 2: One dataset in R and Python](tutorials/02-r-and-python/r-and-python-dataframes.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pub-card}
[Bioinformatics · R]{.pub-year}

[[Modern Statistics for Modern Biology](https://www.huber.embl.de/msmb/)]{.pub-title}

[Susan Holmes and Wolfgang Huber]{.pub-meta}

Statistics for high-throughput biology with R and Bioconductor: multiple testing, clustering, RNA-seq and more.

Goes with: the [chromosome X RNA-seq project](projects/chrx-rnaseq/index.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pub-card}
[Machine learning · Python]{.pub-year}

[[An Introduction to Statistical Learning, with Applications in Python](https://www.statlearning.com/)]{.pub-title}

[Gareth James, Daniela Witten, Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani and Jonathan Taylor]{.pub-meta}

The standard introduction to machine learning: regression, classification, resampling, trees and boosting, with Python labs. The PDF is free on the book's site.

Goes with: the classifier planned for the [TB BAL cytokines project](projects/tb-bal-cytokines/index.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pub-card}
[Machine learning · SHAP]{.pub-year}

[[Interpretable Machine Learning](https://christophm.github.io/interpretable-ml-book/)]{.pub-title}

[Christoph Molnar]{.pub-meta}

How to explain what a model has learnt, including clear chapters on Shapley values and SHAP, permutation importance and partial dependence.

Goes with: the classifier planned for the [TB BAL cytokines project](projects/tb-bal-cytokines/index.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pub-card}
[Python · machine learning]{.pub-year}

[[Python Data Science Handbook](https://jakevdp.github.io/PythonDataScienceHandbook/)]{.pub-title}

[Jake VanderPlas]{.pub-meta}

NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib and scikit-learn in one book. The free online version is the first edition.

Goes with: [Tutorial 2: One dataset in R and Python](tutorials/02-r-and-python/r-and-python-dataframes.qmd) and the [credit risk pipeline](projects/credit-risk-pipeline/index.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pub-card}
[Git · RStudio]{.pub-year}

[[Happy Git and GitHub for the useR](https://happygitwithr.com/)]{.pub-title}

[Jenny Bryan, the STAT 545 TAs and Jim Hester]{.pub-meta}

Setting up Git and GitHub with RStudio, and the everyday version-control habits that keep an analysis reproducible.
:::

:::

## Command line and Linux

Getting comfortable in a terminal, from your first `cd` to building pipelines. Start with my article, [The command line for biologists](writing/command-line-for-biologists/index.qmd), then go further with these.

::: {.grid .resource-grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pub-card}
[Command line · book]{.pub-year}

[[Data Science at the Command Line (2nd edition)](https://jeroenjanssens.com/dsatcl/)]{.pub-title}

[Jeroen Janssens]{.pub-meta}

Obtaining, cleaning, exploring and modelling data with command-line tools and pipes, including tools that understand CSV and JSON. Free to read online.

Goes with: [The command line for biologists](writing/command-line-for-biologists/index.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pub-card}
[Linux · book]{.pub-year}

[[The Linux Command Line](https://linuxcommand.org/tlcl.php)]{.pub-title}

[William Shotts]{.pub-meta}

A complete beginner-to-advanced guide to the Linux shell, from navigating folders to writing shell scripts. The PDF is a free download.

Goes with: [The command line for biologists](writing/command-line-for-biologists/index.qmd)
:::

:::

::: {.grid .resource-grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-sm-6 .g-col-lg-4 .resource-card}
[[The Unix Shell](https://swcarpentry.github.io/shell-novice/)]{.resource-title}

Software Carpentry's hands-on lesson: files, pipes, loops and scripts, with exercises
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-sm-6 .g-col-lg-4 .resource-card}
[[Command Line for Genomics](https://datacarpentry.github.io/shell-genomics/)]{.resource-title}

Data Carpentry's lesson applying the shell to sequencing files
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-sm-6 .g-col-lg-4 .resource-card}
[[The command line for beginners](https://ubuntu.com/tutorials/command-line-for-beginners)]{.resource-title}

Ubuntu's own short tutorial for first-time terminal users
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-sm-6 .g-col-lg-4 .resource-card}
[[The Missing Semester](https://missing.csail.mit.edu/)]{.resource-title}

MIT's free lectures on the shell, scripting, editors and Git
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-sm-6 .g-col-lg-4 .resource-card}
[[Linux command line guide](https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/linux-command-line-bash-tutorial/)]{.resource-title}

freeCodeCamp's long written tutorial on Bash commands
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-sm-6 .g-col-lg-4 .resource-card}
[[explainshell](https://explainshell.com/)]{.resource-title}

Paste a command and see what each part of it does
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-sm-6 .g-col-lg-4 .resource-card}
[[OverTheWire: Bandit](https://overthewire.org/wargames/bandit/)]{.resource-title}

A game that teaches Linux commands one level at a time
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-sm-6 .g-col-lg-4 .resource-card}
[[WSL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install)]{.resource-title}

Running Ubuntu inside Windows, from Microsoft's install guide
:::

:::

## Free courses

Structured, self-paced courses that teach programming and data skills from scratch.

::: {.grid .resource-grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-sm-6 .g-col-lg-4 .resource-card}
[[freeCodeCamp](https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn)]{.resource-title}

Free interactive courses and certifications, including Python and data analysis
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-sm-6 .g-col-lg-4 .resource-card}
[[Software Carpentry](https://software-carpentry.org/lessons/)]{.resource-title}

Lessons on the shell, Git, R and Python for researchers
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-sm-6 .g-col-lg-4 .resource-card}
[[Data Carpentry](https://datacarpentry.org/lessons/)]{.resource-title}

Data skills for researchers, with lesson sets for genomics and ecology
:::

:::

## Bioinformatics

::: {.grid .resource-grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-sm-6 .g-col-lg-4 .resource-card}

[[Nextflow](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/)]{.resource-title}

[[nf-core](https://nf-co.re/)]{.resource-title}

Community-built, peer-reviewed Nextflow pipelines
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-sm-6 .g-col-lg-4 .resource-card}
[[Bioconda](https://bioconda.github.io/)]{.resource-title}

Thousands of bioinformatics command-line tools, installed with conda
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-sm-6 .g-col-lg-4 .resource-card}
[[GATK](https://gatk.broadinstitute.org/hc/en-us)]{.resource-title}

The Broad Institute's toolkit for variant discovery
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-sm-6 .g-col-lg-4 .resource-card}
[[Galaxy Training Network](https://training.galaxyproject.org/)]{.resource-title}

Free hands-on tutorials across genomics and bioinformatics
:::

:::
